newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Andreotti tells Mafia trial: "I'm no angel".
newsitem.headline: Italy's Andreotti tells Mafia trial: "I'm no angel".

text.p: Former Italian prime minister Giulio Andreotti, on trial on charges of associating with the Mafia, said on Monday he knew he was "no angel" but he rejected the evidence of a former mobster.

The seven-times prime minister and life senator sat calmly in a courtroom in Rome's Rebibbia jail as Mafia turncoat Francesco Marino Mannoia testified from behind a screen to having seen Andreotti at a meeting of Mafia bosses in Sicily.
"It's a calumny. There's not even anything new in it," Andreotti later told reporters.

Asked by reporters whether it was simply a case of his word against that of Marino Mannoia, a self-confessed major heroin refiner for the Mob, Andreotti said: "I don't think I am an angel, but I do think I am worth something more than him."
Marino Mannoia told the court he saw Andreotti at a meeting of Mafia godfathers in 1980. "My memory is vivid," he said.
Prosecutors allege that the former prime minister was Cosa Nostra's chief protector in the Rome corridors of power.

Andreotti is also on trial in the northern city of Perugia on charges of complicity in the murder of a muck-racking journalist who was planning to expose the financing of Andreotti's faction of the now defunct Christian Democrat party.

Marino Mannoia alleged that Mafia "boss of bosses" Salvatore Riina ordered Mafiosi in 1987 to vote for Socialists instead of Christian Democrats as a "slap" to the party "and in particular to Andreotti, who was no longer available for Cosa Nostra".
The Christian Democrat party collapsed in the corruption scandals of the early 1990s.
Andreotti has denied all charges against him. "The only thing that bothers me is that this story never ends," he told reporters.
